mission: Led by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, CAISI uses the National Research Council and CIFAR to study risks such as synthetic content (impersonation, fraud) and systems that may be dangerous or hinder human oversight. CIFAR's CAISI Research Program funds investigator-led research, while government-directed projects include joint testing with international partners.

key_work.title: What information should AI evaluators share?
key_work.plain_summary: CAISI's first blog post: best practices for reporting AI evaluation results so they are understood, trusted and used responsibly.

key_work.title: Research Agenda on Risks from Synthetic Content
key_work.plain_summary: Sets out research priorities on deepfakes, impersonation and fraud enabled by AI-generated content.

key_work.title: CAISI Research Program at CIFAR – 2025 Year in Review
key_work.plain_summary: In its first year the CIFAR program put C$2.4m into 12 AI-safety projects with 55+ experts.

key_work.title: CIFAR commits $1M to global AI safety initiative
key_work.plain_summary: Four Canadian projects join the UK-led international AI Alignment Project, each receiving up to C$165k per year.

warnings.text: Synthetic content enables impersonation and fraud.
Advanced systems may be dangerous or hinder human oversight.

recommendations.text: Share evaluation information clearly and consistently so results can be trusted.
Fund multidisciplinary, including sociotechnical, AI-safety research.
Coordinate testing with international partners such as UK AISI.
